I had been a member of Reddit for 7 years. The initial draw for me was the wide range of discussions in the various corners of Reddit. For every article on a critical world issue that was posted, I knew I could go into the comments and inevitably read multiple complex interpretations of the event occuring within a dynamic dialogue.

Sure, I was also there for entertainment from time to time, but I primarily used Reddit to be an informed citizen who could navigate a wide variety of opinions on any given issue, which is very important to me. After seeing an /r/Imgoingtohellforthis post turn into a comment graveyard not a day after Pao made those remarks on NPR about making Reddit a "safespace" - which just screams totalitarian censorship to me - and the post on /r/conspiracy about a user being banned from 400+ subreddits in minutes I realized that Reddit will no longer be the place I can get that variety of opinions. Even if I disagree with an opinion or find it offensive I want to see it.

Only one set of opinions will be accepted on Reddit anymore. I am a politician; a philosopher; a student of history, society, and religion; and I hope Voat is the future of directed, uncensored discussion on the internet.
